# Bullet (KPI rows)

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Bullet-graph KPI rows — qualitative bands, dark measure bar, target tick, delta vs target. Type `bullet`.

## Use cases

- KPIs against target
- Plan attainment per unit
- Scorecard of several metrics

## Chart IDs

One form; its chart ID is `bullet`.

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "bullet",
  "data": { "rows": [{ "id": "orders", "label": "Orders", "value": 85, "target": 100 }] },
  "options": {
    "unit": "orders",
    "title": "Orders reach 85 against a target of 100",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| rows | array | yes | KPI rows displayed in the supplied order. |
| rows[].id | string | yes | Unique KPI-row identity used by annotations and scene elements. |
| rows[].label | string |  | Displayed KPI-row name; defaults to its id. |
| rows[].date | string |  | ISO period date for CAGR between same-measure rows on a shared scale. |
| rows[].value | cell | yes | Actual measure drawn as the row bar. |
| rows[].target | cell |  | Reference measure drawn as the target tick and used for target deltas. It uses the row value's format or options.format; a different target.format warns because it is ignored. options.strings.target renames the comparison mark in labels (e.g. 'peer median'). |
| rows[].bands | array |  | Ordered qualitative band thresholds, as numbers or labeled threshold objects. |
| rows[].bands[].tone | string |  | Semantic band tone. Toned bands define a two-sided corridor and set the delta tone for values inside them. One of `'good'`, `'warn'`, `'bad'`, `'neutral'`. |
| rows[].bands[].to | number | yes | Upper endpoint of this qualitative band in the row value units. |
| rows[].bands[].label | string |  | Visible name of this qualitative band. |
| rows[].direction | string |  | Whether a higher measure is favorable when interpreting the target difference. Neutral uses plain ink without a judgment, including when bands have tones. One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`, `'neutral'`. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| labels | false \| object | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | False hides value, target-value and delta labels. Row names remain. category: false hides row names. density: compact draws no labels. |
| axisTitles | object |  |  | Title of the value axis when it is drawn: under the tick row of the shared-scale axis valueAxis.show draws, ending at its right end. Drawn only when authored. |
| axisTitles.primary | string |  |  | 'Measure, unit' title of the value axis, e.g. 'Margin, %'. |
| sharedScale | boolean \| string | `'percentOfTarget'` (or another value of its type) |  | true: one absolute scale across all rows (same-unit rows, comparable magnitudes; supports valueAxis). false: each row normalized to its own zero-based extent — band maximum extended by value/target overshoot; a bandless row uses its value/target extent (the bullet-graph percent-of-scale — mixed-unit KPI rows stay legible; valueAxis is ignored with a warning). 'percentOfTarget': every row in percent of its own target (actual ÷ target) on one 0–120% scale, three shared bands named once in a key (below 80%, 80–100%, at or above target), mirrored at 100% on a lower-is-better row (the key then reads more than 20% off, up to 20% off, on target or better), one target line at 100%, value, share of target and delta beside each row; the rows' bands, valueAxis and annotations are not drawn. Default: false when every row declares bands and the rows differ in unit or band thresholds (warns bullet-row-scales), true otherwise. |
| bandKey | string | `'auto'`, `'labels'`, `'ramp'`, `'row'` | `'auto'` | How the bands are named. 'labels': one key entry for each band label and shade. 'ramp': one worse-to-better key with one entry for each band (Worse ... Better); it needs the same 2 to 5 bands on every banded row, no band tone and no neutral row, and otherwise keeps labels with a warning. 'row': each band's name prints above its band on every row, as authored, in a lighter band ramp (0.06 lightness steps); on per-row scales the band edges are ticked and numbered under each row; the value sits just past the bar end; a key at the bottom names the bar (Actual), the target tick and, where it applies, the ramp. It needs a name on every band, rows side by side with the target column, and room for each name above its band; otherwise the key names the bands with a warning. 'auto': 'row' for at most 4 rows that name every band wherever it can show; else the ramp when rows run both directions, a label sits on more than one shade and the ramp can apply; otherwise labels. Default 'auto'. The percentOfTarget scale has its own key. |
| targetColumns | boolean |  | `true` | true: where the rows sit side by side and the plot keeps 45% of the width, a Target column and a Gap-to-target column print beside the rows, each under a head, with the gap's position (below, above or on target) under it and the row's direction (higher or lower is better) under its name. Where they do not fit, the target prints above its tick and the delta at the row end. false: always the second form. Default true. The percentOfTarget scale has its own columns. |
| density | string | `'compact'`, `'regular'` | `'regular'` | 'compact' is the 120 x 28 text-free mark: bar, bands and target tick, no labels, axis or key. The percentOfTarget scale needs a key and a value column, so compact refuses it. 'regular' uses labelled stacked rows when side columns take too much plot width. Height depends on row count and text. Default 'regular'. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis.tickStep`, `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `valueAxis.break`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `sort`, `topN`, `hatchStrength`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. |
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. An arrow's ends show its span, so an arrow prints the rate alone unless period is true. shape: bracket \| arrow, default bracket. arrow draws one straight arrow over the marks with the rate in an oval on it, lifted until it clears them. Where no straight line clears the chart, the span is too short for the oval, a stack's inner layer is the anchor or the chart lays comparisons out itself, it draws the bracket and warns cagr-arrow-no-room. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |
| valueLine | Draws a reference line at an authored value or an engine-computed mean, with optional tolerance shading and attainment fill between the line and resolved actuals. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) | value: number \| 'mean', default mean. A number draws the line there; mean has the engine compute it. valueKind: 'fraction'. Multiply a numeric value and its tolerance by 100 before layout: 0.35 draws at 35%. Independent of data.valueKind. Omit it for values already in percent points; not valid with mean. label: string \| false. Name plus value; ${value} sets its position. A number already in the name is kept once. false hides it. tolerance: number \| { low, high }. A number shades that distance on both sides of the line; low and high shade an authored corridor. attainment: boolean \| { seriesId, direction }. Shades each category between its actual and the line. | No anchor is required. Value defaults to mean. Scoped means are line-only: seriesId and paired from/to compute a primary-axis mean and limit its stroke to those bands; other types refuse scope fields for a mean. Numeric values cannot use scope fields except as a category clip with tolerance or attainment. A secondary-axis line needs an acknowledged secondary scale and an explicit numeric value. Optional tolerance shades a value-axis band; optional attainment fills between the line and resolved actuals. |
| band | Draws an inclusive category span as a shaded band or bracket, or a value-axis plan corridor, tolerance band or attainment fill, with a collision-managed label. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) |  | Era shade/bracket needs inclusive category IDs. Corridor and tolerance use finite low/high on the value scale, with optional from/to as a category clip. Attainment needs a plan value and shades each resolved actual; missing cells are skipped. Divider applies only to bracket bands. Scenario AC/PY/PL/FC paints a plan corridor (default PL). |

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
